Our side, re-verified 2026-09-24: installSaveWatcher wraps globalThis.fetch ONCE behind a module flag (stHost/persistence.ts:25, :57-77) and observeNextSave never re-checks that the wrapper is still installed (:79); a save the wrapper does not see times out as 'no save request went out' (saveEvidence.ts, recordSaveEvidence), which is sticky (saveHealth.ts) and makes withLedger refuse every effect (effectsApplier.ts). The host shape: any extension that captured window.fetch before us and later puts it back (a common teardown pattern) removes our wrapper from the chain. The fixture reproduces exactly that with a fetch our wrapper never saw, taken from a fresh same-origin iframe. Control first: one consumed line proves the watcher records an applied save. Then the peer 'restores' fetch, a second line is consumed (its boundary persists through saveMetadata), and the outcome of that save is recorded; the page's fetch is put back and one more persist is made BEFORE anything is asserted, so a red run leaves the page healthy. Asserts: the save made while the peer's fetch was installed was observed and recorded as applied. EXPECTED RED on today's code: the observation times out and saveHealth records lastOutcome 'unsaved' with 'no save request went out' although the request went out and answered 200. Green once observeNextSave re-wraps whenever globalThis.fetch is not ours (with the WeakSet de-duplication, mutation check 13).
